title: Grace Periods, Default Limits and Reinstatement Allowances
content:
Credit and Collections maintains these limits for **Patient Payment Plans**. They fix, for each plan term, the grace period on an unpaid installment, the number of consecutive missed installments at which a plan defaults, the notice periods, what happens on the invoices at default, and how often and how long after a default a plan may be reinstated.

## Grace and default

| Term | Grace period (calendar days after the due date) | Consecutive missed installments at which the plan defaults | Past-due cure needs every past-due installment paid in full | Past-due notice within (business days) | Default notice within (business days) | Invoices at default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 2 | Yes | 2 | 2 | resume statement cycle |
| 6-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 2 | Yes | 2 | 2 | resume statement cycle |
| 9-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 2 | Yes | 2 | 2 | resume statement cycle |
| 12-Month Payment Plan | 15 | 2 | Yes | 2 | 2 | resume statement cycle |
| 18-Month Payment Plan | 15 | 3 | Yes | 2 | 2 | final notice immediately |
| 24-Month Extended Payment Plan | 15 | 3 | Yes | 2 | 2 | final notice immediately |

- **Grace period**: the calendar days after an installment's due date before an unpaid installment makes the plan past due.
- **Past-due notice / default notice**: the business days after the plan turns past due, or after it defaults, within which the corresponding notice is sent.
- **Invoices at default**: *resume statement cycle* means the invoices resume the statement cycle at the next unused position; *final notice immediately* means the final notice is issued next.

## Reinstatement allowances

| Term | Reinstatements allowed per plan | Reinstatement window (calendar days after the default date) |
|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Payment Plan | 0 | 0 |
| 6-Month Payment Plan | 1 | 30 |
| 9-Month Payment Plan | 1 | 30 |
| 12-Month Payment Plan | 1 | 30 |
| 18-Month Payment Plan | 1 | 45 |
| 24-Month Extended Payment Plan | 1 | 45 |

A figure of 0 reinstatements means a plan on that term is never reinstated after a default; the 3-Month Payment Plan is the only such term.

## Reading the limits

- On the 12-Month Payment Plan, an installment due on the 5th of a month and still unpaid at the end of the 15-day grace period puts the plan past due (hypothetical dates).
- On the 18-Month Payment Plan two consecutive missed installments do not default the plan; the third consecutive one does.
- A defaulted 6-Month Payment Plan has one reinstatement available, inside 30 calendar days of its default date; once that reinstatement has been used, the count is exhausted.
